summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,030.8 crore, +11% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 10.06% and PAT margin to 0.32%.
summary.overview: Oriental Aromatics delivered its first year above INR 1,000 crore revenue, with Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 282 crore (+12% QoQ, +11% YoY) and volumes up 16% QoQ and 5% YoY. Profitability was squeezed by a three-way shock in raw materials (gum turpentine, CST, alpha-pinene at all-time highs), rupee depreciation, pricing pressure in aroma ingredients, and the Mahad ramp-up drag of 1–1.5% on EBITDA margin. Q4 EBITDA margin recovered to 6.89% from 5.26% in Q3, and the company said it has begun passing through price increases of 25–27% over the prior quarter, with management cautioning that the worst on input costs is not yet over. A final dividend of INR 0.50 per share was recommended.

segments.name: Fragrance and Flavor
segments.commentary: Demand described as healthy on premiumisation, with new customers added domestically and internationally. The benefit of softer fragrance raw material prices has largely tapered off as input costs firmed in H2 and especially Q4, which will weigh on profitability in coming quarters.

segments.name: Aroma Ingredients
segments.commentary: Market remains a buyer's market with Chinese capacity flowing into India, Southeast Asia and parts of Europe, keeping end-product prices subdued. Gum turpentine, CST and alpha-pinene costs are at all-time highs, and the division absorbed the input cost shock.

segments.name: Camphor and Terpene Chemicals (Bareilly)
segments.commentary: Bareilly ran at healthy utilisation through the year; Q4 was seasonally soft. Indian camphor is in oversupply, with domestic capacity additions and natural camphor imports from China pressuring prices. Retail focus continues under Saraswati and 3 Pine brands.

segments.name: Mahad (Oriental Aromatics & Sons Ltd, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still ramping up and a 1–1.5% drag on consolidated EBITDA margin. Commercial shipments have started after sampling with several global customers, and the company is qualified to bid for certain global RFQs for H2 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to return EBITDA margin to the guided ~10% level, but says the timing depends on how customers handle price increases in a buyer's market; it described the worst on input costs as not yet over.
Mahad expected to reach 75–80% utilisation within about one year, at which point management expects it to be EBITDA neutral and then contributing.
Mahad full-capacity incremental revenue: management gave INR 50 crore as a conservative FY27 figure, and INR 60–65 crore at optimum utilisation after price increases.
Management declined to give FY27 top-line guidance, prioritising profit preservation over volume growth.
Final dividend of INR 0.50 per share recommended, subject to AGM approval.
Price increases of 25–27% versus a quarter earlier are being passed through in tranches every three months, with monthly price lists for spot sales.
capex_capacity: Mahad dedicated plant investment is about INR 70–75 crore after excluding common infrastructure (plot development, utilities of INR 20–27 crore); total outlay quoted at about INR 90 crore.
Mahad capacity can reportedly be doubled with an additional INR 12–15 crore of capex.
Most plants run at 80–90% utilisation, which management says is needed to cover overheads.
Company is in consolidation mode, focused on extracting benefits from investments made over the past five years; expansion is open to ideas but not the current priority.
Management said maximum turnover at current realisations should be about INR 1,200–1,250 crore, but declined to give a firm number.
demand_pricing: Aroma ingredient pricing remains subdued from Chinese overcapacity; the company is nonetheless seeing constructive RFQ volumes for H2 FY26 with pricing still tight.
Management said US tariff overhang has eased, which should support a gradual recovery in North American order flow.
Price increases of 25–27% versus a quarter earlier are being passed to customers, with customer resistance in a buyer's market.
Indian camphor is in oversupply due to domestic capacity additions, with natural camphor imports from China a secondary factor; management is in dialogue with the government on imports.

Working capital: receivables rose about 40% versus revenue up about 11%, which management attributed to extended credit terms requested by top global customers; some inventory was built up in the past 1.5–2 months to hedge petro-stream availability.

qa_highlights.question: Steps taken to curb natural camphor imports and any government representation on import duty.
qa_highlights.answer: Management has initiated dialogue with the central government twice and is discussing at other levels; it noted imports from China fell versus the last two years. It declined to comment on GST-related issues raised by a participant.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue at full utilisation excluding and including Mahad at current realisations.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave INR 1,200–1,250 crore as achievable maximum turnover at current realisations, excluding a firm figure. Mahad adds about INR 50 crore at current capacity, with INR 60–65 crore at optimum utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate high on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said standalone tax rate is 25%, and the consolidated rate is similar; the higher reported figure reflects the subsidiary's loss (Mahad) not receiving tax benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Q2 and Q4 seasonally stronger than Q1 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the premise: Q2 and Q3 are the strong festive quarters, Q1 is the ramp-up, and Q4 is seasonally slow with subdued sales and promotions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are EBITDA margins (~6%) below FY25 levels (10%) and below peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a three-way input cost shock, rupee depreciation, pricing pressure in aroma ingredients and the Mahad drag; it declined to comment on peers and said a 10% margin is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital build-up: receivables up ~40%, SME dues up from INR 5 crore to ~INR 22 crore, and possible inventory gains; Mahad capex and asset turn.
qa_highlights.answer: Extended credit was given at the request of top customers, with prices adjusted to cover financing cost. Inventory was built to secure petro-stream supply. Mahad dedicated plant capex is about INR 70–75 crore; the CFO cited INR 60–65 crore of optimum revenue, an implied asset turn near 0.8–0.9x.

qa_highlights.question: When will Mahad turn EBITDA neutral and what utilisation is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 75–80% utilisation within the next year, which should make Mahad EBITDA neutral and then contributing, supported by gradual price gains and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company differentiating beyond price against Chinese aroma producers in Europe and South Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited backward integration into fragrance, multi-chemistry expertise across three plants for process and quality gains, and a broad product basket.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic share of revenue risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Global aroma ingredient business has contracted on pricing pressure, while the fragrance division has won significant local business across customer segments.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (gum turpentine, CST, alpha-pinene, crude derivatives) and rupee depreciation may keep margins compressed for several quarters.
Pass-through of 25–27% price increases in a buyer's market; customer resistance could delay margin recovery.
Working capital strain: receivables up ~40% vs revenue +11%, SME payables rising from INR 5 crore to ~INR 22 crore, and inventory build-up.
Mahad ramp-up: EBITDA drag of 1–1.5% persists until 75–80% utilisation, expected within about a year; sample-to-commercial cycles run 6–9 months.
Camphor oversupply in India and Chinese natural camphor imports; policy outcome from government dialogue is uncertain.
No FY27 revenue guidance; management prioritises profit preservation over volume.
summary.management_tone: Confident about the franchise and long-term positioning, but cautious on near-term margins: management repeatedly said headwinds will take several quarters to work through and that the worst on input costs is not over. It was evasive on peer comparisons, camphor policy specifics, and FY27 top-line numbers, calling these "crystal ball" questions.
key_quotes: We are of the opinion that the situation will worsen before we can see some normalcy coming back in pricing of the inputs.
So, it will be our endeavor to go back to the guided number of around 10%.
I think since we are in the buyer's market, there has been substantial resistance from the customers to go and increase the price.
So, we are positive, we are optimistic but we also are realistic because I feel the worst is still not over in terms of the impact of the geopolitical situation on the costs of the products.
Actually, a crystal ball question, Nishita.

adds.what: Mahad (Oriental Aromatics & Sons) dedicated plant, ramping up; commercial shipments started, capacity can be doubled with INR 12-15 crore additional capex

growth.why: Management declined FY27 top-line guidance, prioritising margin recovery to ~10% (endeavour); Mahad incremental revenue of INR 50 crore (conservative FY27) backed by a ramp-up with 75-80% utilisation targeted within a year, while the company is in consolidation mode and expansion not a priority.
